newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No charges against Netanyahu - official.
newsitem.headline: No charges against Netanyahu - official.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will not face charges in a corruption scandal, his spokesman said on Sunday.

But the future of his government hung in the balance as he waited to see how political allies would react to the findings of prosecutors who examined his handling of a short-lived appointment of an attorney general.

Asked if it was correct the Israeli leader would not be indicted, his communications chief David Bar-Illan told Reuters: "That's right." The report, first delivered to Netanyahu and other suspects, was due to be made public later in the day.

A government official said only one of the four officials who police recommended be charged over the short-lived appointment of an attorney general would be indicted -- Shas party leader and coalition ally Aryeh Deri.

"Also the language is only very mildly critical as far as I know. I haven't been able to read the whole thing yet. But from the report I got, it's a very mild criticism. I have looked at it cursorily," the official said.
"Both (Justice Minister) Tzachi Hanegbi and the prime minister are completely in the clear on the ministerial level," the official told Reuters.

Israeli media reports had speculated Netanyahu would not be charged but said the findings could be critical of his handling of the appointment in January of Likud political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general.

The 47-year-old Likud party leader, elected 11 months ago on a promise to pursue peace with security, last week became the first Israeli prime minister to face a police recommendation he be brought to trial -- on charges of fraud and breach of trust.

Police recommended the prime minister and officials be indicted in connection with the appointment of Bar-On, who quit 12 hours after taking office amid strong public criticism that he was a legal lightweight unfit for the job.
Israel's Channel One television sparked the investigation by alleging that Deri, a Netanyahu ally on trial for corruption, promoted Bar-On for the job in the hope of winning a plea bargain.
The television said Deri had promised that in return, his Shas party would support Netanyahu's deal with the Palestinians to pull back Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Police also recommended charges be brought against Deri, Hanegbi and the prime minister's director-general Avigdor Lieberman. All denied any wrongdoing.
Netanyahu was expected to address the nation after the prosecutors announce their report.
Netanyahu could still face a rebellion from cabinet ministers who could topple his coalition government if the findings raised serious questions about his integrity.

The scandal has cast a giant shadow over Middle East peacemaking, already in crisis since Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month and sparked an outburst of violence.

"If mistakes were made here, they were routine political mistakes that were made by governments in the past," Bar-Illan said. "But what that has to do with any kind of criminal investigation, or let alone indictment, I don't know."
He acknowledged the affair would sap some of the government's energies for a few weeks but did not believe peacemaking would be unduly harmed.
Netanyahu's coalition of mainly right-wing and religious parties holds 66 seats in the 120-member parliament.
Even though Netanyahu is not indicted, the opposition can ask Israel's High Court of Justice to force charges to be brought based on the evidence.
